title: Derived base change for ring cotangent complexes
statement: Let $A\to C$, $A\to A'$, $C\to C'$ and $A'\to C'$ be a commutative square of homomorphisms of commutative rings. Write $D(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T))$ for the derived category of ordinary $T$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and compute derived tensor products using flat resolutions. Assume that the canonical multiplication map $\mu:C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C'[0]$ induced by this square is a quasi-isomorphism in $D(A')$. For the standard cotangent complexes and their square-induced functoriality maps [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], the canonical $C'$-linear base-change morphism $\beta:L_{C/A}\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\longrightarrow L_{C'/A'}$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$. Here $\beta$ is the derived extension-of-scalars adjoint of the functoriality morphism $L_{C/A}\to L_{C'/A'}$, where the target of the latter is viewed as a complex of $C$-modules via $C\to C'$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), with the commutative square equation-commutative-square and its functoriality map in section-functoriality. The hypothesis is the canonical derived-tensor quasi-isomorphism, as applied in Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence).

proof.text: Write $f:C\to C'$ for the square's given map. Take $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C/A)$ from [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Apply [lem-trf-derived-square-polynomial-resolution] to the given square and its canonical $\mu$. The hypothesis makes $\alpha:C\otimes_A A'\to C'$ an isomorphism and makes $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'$, augmented by $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$, a polynomial resolution of $C'$ over $A'$. This uses the derived-tensor hypothesis itself, without assuming a flat ring map.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof using the free resolution s(P) and its tensor augmentation; the degree-zero pushout identification makes explicit the reduction for a general commutative square.

proof.text: Put $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}C)$ and $K'=s(\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/A'}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}C')$. By [lem-trf-polynomial-differential-base-change], $K$ has flat terms, is K-flat, and $\Theta=Q(\theta)c_K:QK\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\xrightarrow{\sim}QK'$ is the isomorphism represented by $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'\mapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'$. Since $P_\bullet$ is the standard resolution, [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] identifies $QK=L_{C/A}$ by definition; the resolution from Step 1 has a canonical comparison isomorphism $c_{P'}:QK'\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{C'/A'}$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), proof: flatness of the polynomial differential module and its identification after scalar extension, written in the alternating polynomial-resolution model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-base-change-adjunct-formula]: Step 1 supplies its polynomial-resolution hypothesis and Step 2 its K-flatness and flat terms. Write $R_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C'/A')$ and $h:P'_\bullet\to R_\bullet$, $p\otimes a'\mapsto t(p)a'$, where $t$ is the square-induced standard map. The cited formula uses $c_RQK(h)=c_{P'}$ and the same normalized computation map $c_K$ as Step 2 to identify the adjunct of the specified functoriality map, hence the $\beta$ in the statement, with $c_RQK(h)Q(\theta)c_K=c_{P'}\Theta$. The two factors $c_{P'}$ and $\Theta$ are isomorphisms by Step 2. Therefore the canonical $\beta$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), the standard-resolution map and its differential formula; Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), identifying the induced morphism by scalar-extension adjunction.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), using the explicit polynomial-resolution model of Tags 08QI/08QL and the resolution argument of Tag 08QP. The polynomial-module identification and canonical adjunct are written out.
